changed.statement: ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), 2 ≤ n → 2 ≤ m → (∀ u u' : Fin n, u ≠ u' → ∃ v, A u v = true ∧ A u' v = false) → (∀ v v' : Fin m, v ≠ v' → ∃ u, A u v = true ∧ A u v' = false) → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C → n + m - 1 ≤ C.size

changed.context: Every ordered pair of unequal rows and every such pair of columns can be distinguished in each direction. Count effective input uses in the output cone.
changed.sketch: Prune gates outside the output cone and normalize each NOT to the operand it uses. Two unread rows would have identical outputs. With one unread row, every other row input can raise or lower the output on suitable columns, so it needs two paths. Count repeated wire uses when one coordinate is unread on each side. Analyze a cone with exactly one repeated wire to exclude two independently two-way inputs. Compare the effective wire count with fan-in two. Test the identity graph for equality.

changed.title: Sharp support bound and equality cases for the Walsh spectrum of a triangular Boolean product circuit
changed.statement:
∀ t : ℕ,
  let V := Fin t → ZMod 2
  ∀ (A B : Fin t → Fin t → ZMod 2) (γ : V),
    let sources := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin t)).filter (fun j =>
      ∃ i, j < i ∧ (A i j ≠ 0 ∨ B i j ≠ 0))
    let c := fun (j : Fin t) (z : V × V) =>
      γ j + ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ioi j, (z.1 i * A i j + z.2 i * B i j)
    let live := (Finset.univ : Finset (V × V)).filter (fun z =>
      ∀ j, c j z ≠ 0 ∨ (z.1 j = 0 ∧ z.2 j = 0))
    let lhs := 2 * 4^sources.card * live.card
    let rhs := (4^sources.card + 1) * 4^t
    lhs ≤ rhs ∧
      (lhs = rhs ↔
        (∀ j, j ∉ sources → γ j = 1) ∧
        ∀ j ∈ sources, ∀ k ∈ sources, ∀ z, c j z = c k z)
changed.unlocks: determines the extremal support count and equality conditions for the triangular coefficient test at each number of feedback sources
changed.context: A source j kills a frequency when its later affine coefficient vanishes and its own pair is nonzero. The initial event has probability 1/2. Process sources downwards. The union U already killed depends only on later pairs, so its new measure is at least 3/8+Pr(U)/4. Equality at each update requires all later killed events to lie in the current zero hyperplane. Each such event spans its own hyperplane since the three nonzero local pairs span the two-bit affine plane. A zero sink coefficient kills 3/4. Allow 2 to 4 hours.

changed.title: The optimal worst-case success and largest seed weight for randomized fan-in-two inner-product predictors
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false,false]) (g.op.eval [false,true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true,false]) (g.op.eval [true,true]))
∀ s t : ℕ, t ≤ s →
  let N := 2^(2*s)
  let h : ℕ := 2^(s-t)
  let valid := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (N+N) C ∧ C.gates.countP nonlinear ≤ t
  let value := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (x y : Fin N) =>
    C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach x y)
  let target := fun (i j : Fin N) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (2*s))).filter (fun b =>
      i.val.testBit b.val && j.val.testBit b.val)).card % 2 == 1
  (∀ (l : ℕ) (Cs : Fin l → PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (p : Fin l → ℚ),
    (∀ i, valid (Cs i)) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ p i) → (∑ i, p i) = 1 →
    let success := fun (x y : Fin N) =>
      ∑ i : Fin l, if value (Cs i) x y = target x y then p i else 0
    (∃ x y, 2*(h : ℚ)*success x y ≤ (h : ℚ)+1) ∧
    ((∀ x y, (h : ℚ)+1 ≤ 2*(h : ℚ)*success x y) →
      ∀ i, (h : ℚ)^2 * p i ≤ 1)) ∧
  ∃ Cs : Fin (h^2) → PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, (∀ z, valid (Cs z)) ∧
    ∀ x y, 2*h*((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (h^2))).filter
      (fun z => value (Cs z) x y = target x y)).card = (h+1)*h^2
changed.unlocks: prices the minimum support of a finite lottery attaining optimal prediction probability on each inner-product input
changed.context: Use affine port labels to bound the sign matrix rank by m. Project H onto the range of each prediction. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds correlation and saturation gives K_i=h P_i H. Pointwise equality yields a tight weighted sum of projections. Apply the projection weight bound to get mass at most one over h squared on each positive atom. Pair dot coordinates with one product per pair, then translate the residual columns uniformly and add the local row correction. This attains the stated bias on every cell. Allow 3 to 5 hours.

changed.title: A sharp three-eighths threshold for perturbing column multiplicities in even-rank zero-parity pairings
changed.statement:
∀ (r c e : ℕ), 2 ≤ r → Even r →
  let V := Fin r → ZMod 2
  let n := c * 2^r
  4*e ≤ 3*n →
  ∀ x : Fin n → V,
    (∀ v : V, (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => x i = v)).card = c) →
    let deficit := fun (y : Fin n → V) =>
      ∑ v : V, (c - (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => y i = v)).card)
    let zeroBox := fun (y : Fin n → V) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (K : Finset (Fin n)) =>
      ∀ i ∈ K, ∀ j ∈ K, dotProduct (x i - x j) (y (π i) - y (π j)) = 0
    let upper := max (n-e) (n/4+e)
    (∀ y : Fin n → V, deficit y = e →
      (∃ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (K : Finset (Fin n)), zeroBox y π K ∧ K.card = n-e) ∧
      (∀ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (K : Finset (Fin n)), zeroBox y π K → K.card ≤ upper)) ∧
    (∃ (y : Fin n → V), deficit y = e ∧
      ∃ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (K : Finset (Fin n)), zeroBox y π K ∧ K.card = upper)
changed.unlocks: locates the sharp histogram threshold for zero-parity pairings at positive uniform row multiplicity in even dimension
changed.context: An invertible alternating map pairs c rows per type, retaining N-e. A proper affine row span retains at most N/2. Full row span forces a graph of an alternating map. An invertible map retains at most N-e. A singular map in even dimension loses at least two ranks, so its column flat holds at most N/4+e names. For sharpness use an alternating map with a two-dimensional kernel. Move e labels from outside its image into that flat, allowing at most 4c per image type. Exactly N/4+e columns there can now be paired.

changed.title: An affine column flat with singleton or paired bins prices zero-parity matchings against uniform binary row types
changed.statement:
∀ (r c t : ℕ),
  let V := Fin r → ZMod 2
  let n := c * 2^r
  ∀ (x y : Fin n → V),
    (∀ v : V, (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => x i = v)).card = c) →
    ((∃ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (K : Finset (Fin n)), n ≤ K.card + t ∧
      ∀ i ∈ K, ∀ j ∈ K, dotProduct (x i - x j) (y (π i) - y (π j)) = 0) ↔
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (W : Finset V) (a δ : V),
      d ≤ r ∧ W.card = 2^d ∧ 0 ∈ W ∧ (∀ v ∈ W, ∀ w ∈ W, v+w ∈ W) ∧
      δ ∈ W ∧ (δ = 0 ↔ Even d) ∧
      let bins := W.image (fun w => ({a+w, a+w+δ} : Finset V))
      n ≤ t + ∑ bin ∈ bins,
        min (c * 2^(r-d)) (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => y i ∈ bin)).card)
changed.unlocks: computes the maximum zero-parity physical pairing size from affine-bin capacities when every row type has uniform multiplicity
changed.context: Subtract a matched origin. Zero boxes give a singular relation. On its row projection U, pairing a row lift with another row defines an alternating form. Write K for its radical. Column types lie in a translate of the annihilator of K, in bins modulo the annihilator of U. Each bin has c times the size of K compatible rows. The quotient has even rank, so refine the bin directions to dimension zero or one without reducing capacity. Conversely a symplectic basis on the even-dimensional quotient realizes these bins and their caps. Match within bins.

changed.title: An ordinary two-state integer matrix product computes one cyclic Walsh transition over all lifts of its input mask
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] (d : ℕ),
  let I := ZMod k
  let B := ZMod 2
  let V := I → B
  let sign := fun (t : B) => if t = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1
  let mix := fun (x : V) (i : I) => x (i-(d : I)) + x i + x (i+(d : I))
  let nl := fun (y : V) (j : I) => y j + (1+y (j+1))*y (j+2)
  let lifts := fun (a : V) => Finset.univ.filter (fun u : V => mix u = a)
  let transfer := fun (u b : V) (j : ℕ) =>
    let i := (j : I)
    (fun (left right : B) =>
      sign ((u i+b i+b (i-2))*left + b (i-1)*left*right) : Matrix B B ℤ)
  let g := Nat.gcd k d
  ∀ (a b : V),
    (∑ x : V, sign (dotProduct a x + dotProduct b (nl (mix x)))) =
      ∑ u ∈ lifts a, Matrix.trace (List.prod (α := Matrix B B ℤ) ((List.range k).map (transfer u b))) ∧
    (lifts a).card = (if (∃ y : V, mix y = a) then
      (if 3 ∣ (k/g) then 4^g else 1) else 0)
changed.unlocks: Supplies the single-round character coefficients for the two scheduled words and their shared raw key, including widths at which the three-tap mix is singular.
changed.context: Expand the signed exponent on each cyclic edge. With each transfer typed as an integer matrix, matrix multiplication sums the shared Boolean state. Taking its trace closes the cycle. Sum over the lifts of the input mask. Orthogonality eliminates inconsistent masks. The three-tap recurrence on each d-orbit repeats u,v,u+v, giving four kernel words precisely when the orbit length is divisible by three.

changed.title: Ordinary matrix transfers of two cyclic words recover the exact joint Walsh sums and key counts through the common reinjection schedule
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] (r : ℕ),
  let I := ZMod k
  let B := ZMod 2
  let V := I → B
  let N := (2:ℤ)^k
  let sign := fun (t : B) => if t = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (word : V) (i : I) => word (i-(s : I))
  let back := fun (s : ℕ) (b : V) (i : I) => b (i+(s : I))
  let mix := fun (d : ℕ) (x : V) (i : I) => x (i-(d : I)) + x i + x (i+(d : I))
  let nl := fun (y : V) (j : I) => y j + (1+y (j+1))*y (j+2)
  let kernel := fun (d : ℕ) (a b : V) =>
    ∑ u ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun v : V => mix d v = a),
      Matrix.trace (List.prod (α := Matrix B B ℤ) ((List.range k).map (fun j =>
        let i := (j : I)
        (fun (l h : B) => sign ((u i+b i+b (i-2))*l+b (i-1)*l*h) : Matrix B B ℤ))))
  ∀ (row col : V) (C : ℕ → V),
    let orbit := fun (key : V) =>
      (List.range r).foldl (fun (st : V × V) tick =>
        (nl (mix 1 st.1) + rot (2*tick) key + C (tick+1),
         nl (mix 2 st.2) + rot (3*(tick+1)+1) key + C (r+tick+1)))
        (rot 1 key + row, rot 3 key + col)
    let initial := fun (a b q : V) =>
      if q + back 1 a + back 3 b = 0 then N*sign (dotProduct a row + dotProduct b col) else 0
    let H := (List.range r).foldl (fun (old : V → V → V → ℤ) roundIndex p s t =>
      sign (dotProduct p (C (roundIndex+1)) + dotProduct s (C (r+roundIndex+1))) *
        ∑ a : V, ∑ b : V, kernel 1 a p * kernel 2 b s *
          old a b (t + back (2*roundIndex) p + back (3*(roundIndex+1)+1) s)) initial
    (∀ a b q : V, H a b q = N^(2*r) *
      ∑ w : V, sign (dotProduct a (orbit w).1 + dotProduct b (orbit w).2 + dotProduct q w)) ∧
    ∀ (S T : Finset I) (y z : V),
      let supported := fun (sites : Finset I) => Finset.univ.filter (fun mask : V =>
        ∀ i : I, i ∉ sites → mask i = 0)
      let passing := Finset.univ.filter (fun w : V =>
        (∀ i ∈ S, (orbit w).1 i = y i) ∧ (∀ j ∈ T, (orbit w).2 j = z j))
      (∑ a ∈ supported S, ∑ b ∈ supported T,
        sign (dotProduct a y + dotProduct b z) * H a b 0) =
        N^(2*r) * (2:ℤ)^(S.card+T.card) * (passing.card : ℤ)
changed.unlocks: Recovers the distinct key count for arbitrary selected sites of both scheduled words through any number of rounds.
changed.context: Import the corrected single-round matrix transfer. Expand each physical row in Walsh characters, one factor per schedule. Rotation moves each injection mask back to the same raw-key frequency. Induct on the round count and track the two inversion factors N per round. Character orthogonality on the selected output positions gives the final key count. At width two and zero masks the one-round scaled joint moment is 64.

changed.title: One key parity chosen from the observed output cannot repair the whole four-round shift-12 graph row at width seventeen
changed.statement:
let k : Nat := 17
let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
  ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
  (List.range k).foldl (fun acc b =>
    acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit b)
      (!(word.testBit ((b + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((b + 2) % k))).toNat <<< b)) 0
let output := fun (w : Nat) =>
  ((List.range 4).foldl (fun x t =>
    step (x ^^^ rot 1 x ^^^ rot (k - 1) x) ^^^ rot (2 * t) w ^^^
      (3 ^ (k + (t + 1)) % 2 ^ k)) (rot 1 w)) >>> 8
let columnPass := fun (key name : Nat) =>
  ((List.range 4).foldl (fun state j =>
    step (state ^^^ rot 2 state ^^^ rot (k - 2) state) ^^^
      rot (3 * (j + 1) + 1) key ^^^ (3 ^ (k + (4 + (j + 1))) % 2 ^ k))
    (rot 3 key ^^^ name)) < 2 ^ 8
let keys := List.range (2 ^ k)
let edge := fun (column : Nat) => ∃ w ∈ keys, output w = 0 ∧ columnPass w column
let parity := fun (mask word : Nat) =>
  ((List.range k).filter (fun i => mask.testBit i && word.testBit i)).length % 2 == 1
∀ (query : Nat → Fin (2 ^ k)) (lookup : Nat → Bool → Bool),
  let predicted := fun (column : Nat) =>
    ∃ w ∈ keys,
      (if w.testBit 2 then output w = 0
       else
         let probe := w ^^^ 12
         let y := output probe
         lookup y (parity (query y).val probe) = true) ∧ columnPass w column
  edge 0 ∧ (¬predicted 0 ∨ ∃ c : Fin (2 ^ k), ¬edge c.val ∧ predicted c.val)

changed.title: One packed cyclic nonlinear round agrees with every scalar lane for arbitrary input states and additive words
changed.statement:
∀ (k lanes gap : Nat) (hk : 0 < k), gap ≤ k →
  let word := Fin (2 ^ k)
  let atSite := fun j : Nat => (⟨j % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s x : Nat) =>
    ((x <<< (s % k)) ||| (x >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (raw : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc b =>
      acc ||| ((xor (raw.testBit b)
        (!(raw.testBit ((b + 1) % k)) && raw.testBit ((b + 2) % k))).toNat <<< b)) 0
  ∀ (state addend : Fin lanes → word) (planes additions : Fin k → Nat),
    (∀ i w, (planes i).testBit w.val = (state w).val.testBit i.val) →
    (∀ i w, (additions i).testBit w.val = (addend w).val.testBit i.val) →
    let mix := fun j : Nat =>
      planes (atSite j) ^^^ planes (atSite (j + k - gap % k)) ^^^
        planes (atSite (j + gap))
    let full := 2 ^ lanes - 1
    ∀ (i : Fin k) (w : Fin lanes),
      (mix i.val ^^^ ((full ^^^ mix (i.val + 1)) &&& mix (i.val + 2)) ^^^
        additions i).testBit w.val =
      (step ((state w).val ^^^ rot gap (state w).val ^^^ rot (k - gap) (state w).val) ^^^
        (addend w).val).testBit i.val
changed.unlocks: Supplies the round induction in the scalar correspondence for all scheduled row and column certificate computations, independently of initial key-mask arithmetic.
changed.context: For each scalar rotation split the site below or above the reduced shift. Exactly one shifted part can contribute there and the width mask preserves the low bit. The two rotations read j-gap and j+gap cyclically. Reading a lane commutes with XOR and AND, and the full packed mask has a one there. In the scalar OR fold only the shifted Boolean at the requested site can set that bit. Apply the packed addend hypothesis last. The argument includes coincident neighbors. See packed-rounds.md at 1de61e3a54.

changed.title: The repeated binary tile for a translated key coordinate selects exactly the prescribed lanes at every width
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) (shift : Fin (2 ^ k)),
  let lanes := 2 ^ k
  let full := 2 ^ lanes - 1
  let run := 2 ^ i.val
  let tile := ((2 ^ run - 1) <<< run) * (full / (2 ^ (2 * run) - 1))
  let plane := if shift.val.testBit i.val then full ^^^ tile else tile
  ∀ lane : ℕ, plane.testBit lane =
    (decide (lane < lanes) && (lane ^^^ shift.val).testBit i.val)
changed.unlocks: Supplies the initial key-coordinate equality used in every round of the packed proof for the scheduled row and column rules.
changed.context: Put r=2^i, B=2^(2r) and m=2^(k-i-1). There are 2rm lanes. The quotient of B^m-1 by B-1 is the geometric sum. Multiplication by C=2^r(2^r-1) repeats digit C in base B. Induct by appending a digit, x to Bx+C. Since C<B, the low 2r bits come from C and the rest from x. The high half of each block has lane bit i set, and all bits beyond 2rm vanish. XOR with the full mask changes only legal lanes. See packed-rounds.md at 33e7091c2b.

changed.title: Independent flips in symbol pairs bound simultaneous polynomial prediction on permutations of binary words
changed.statement:
∀ w : ℕ,
  let K := ZMod 2
  let V := Fin (w+1) → K
  let I := V × Fin (w+1)
  let s := 2^w
  ∀ (A : Finset V) (c : V → Finset I → K),
    let m := A.card
    let pred := fun (p : Equiv.Perm V) (a : V) =>
      ∑ S ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Finset I)).filter (fun S => S.card ≤ w),
        c a S * ∏ j ∈ S, p j.1 j.2
    let bad := (Finset.univ : Finset (Equiv.Perm V)).filter (fun p =>
      ∃ a ∈ A, pred p a ≠ ∏ i : Fin (w+1), p a i)
    let total := 2^s * Nat.choose (2*s) m
    let empty := ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (s+1), Nat.choose s j * Nat.choose (2*j) m
    Nat.factorial (2*s) * (total - empty) ≤ s * total * bad.card
changed.unlocks: A quantitative joint-error bound on arbitrary marked permutation blocks.
changed.context: Under a common prefix shift and independent last-bit pair flips, summing a predictor over shifts leaves a value independent of flips. Correctness on all shifts prescribes one flip per occupied prefix. For h occupied prefixes at most a 2^(-h) fraction of flip masks succeeds on all shifts. Average over the base permutation and count uniform marked subsets contained in random unions of pairs.

changed.title: A logarithmic binary rank forces crossed parity errors on every matching covering half the types
changed.statement:
∀ coreBits : ℕ, 16 ≤ coreBits →
  let n := 2^coreBits
  let h := n/2
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin (32*coreBits) → F
  ∃ u v : Fin n → W,
    ∀ (row col : Fin h ↪ Fin n) (q : ℕ), 256*coreBits*3^q ≤ n →
    ∀ (color : Fin h → Fin (3^q)) (sign : Fin h → F),
      let dot := fun (x y : W) => ∑ j : Fin (32*coreBits), x j * y j
      let bad := ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin h × Fin h)).filter (fun z =>
        z.1 < z.2 ∧ color z.1 = color z.2 ∧
          dot (u (row z.1)) (v (col z.2)) + dot (u (row z.2)) (v (col z.1)) ≠
            sign z.1 + sign z.2)).card
      h^2 < 4096*3^q*bad
changed.unlocks: The bound applies after keeping arbitrary halves of the two banks, which makes error density survive replication at an absolute constant.
changed.context: Use columns with 8a independent vectors in each 32a-set. Fix both injections, colors and signs. In classes of size at least h/(4C), sample 32a testers, C=3^q. At least h/2 other rows give M≥4ah independent fair tests after conditioning. A low-loss book gives sampled loss ≤ah/8 with chance at least half. Weight the binomial sum at 1/16; (17/16)^8<2 gives a tail ≤2^(-3ah). There are at most n^(2h) C^h 2^h configurations per q, with C≤n/4. The union over at most a+1 budgets has probability below one.

changed.title: Optimal translated prediction menus and the inputs that force their labels
changed.statement:
∀ (m r : Nat),
  let A := Fin (m+1)
  let W := Fin r → Bool
  ∀ label : Fin m → A → W,
    let ok := fun (x : Fin m → W) (a : A) => ∀ i, x i ≠ label i a
    let covers := ∀ x, ∃ a, ok x a
    (covers ↔ ∀ i, Function.Injective (label i)) ∧
    (covers → ∀ b : A, ∃ order : Fin m → A,
      Function.Injective order ∧ (∀ i, order i ≠ b) ∧
      ∀ (flags : Fin m → Bool) (v : A),
        ok (fun pos => label pos (if flags pos then b else order pos)) v ↔
          (v = b ∧ ∀ j, flags j = false) ∨ (∃ j, flags j = true ∧ v = order j))
changed.unlocks: Identifies the minimum-size covering menus and the inputs forcing each label.
changed.context: A collision kills two labels with one coordinate. Use the remaining m-1 coordinates to kill the other labels. With injective columns one input kills at most m labels. To force b, assign the other m labels bijectively to the coordinates and use their forbidden symbols. At any chosen coordinates switch to the symbol for b. If any switch occurs, b is killed and precisely the displaced labels survive, by column injectivity.

changed.title: A maximal Boolean monomial controls projected failures of simultaneous local predictions
changed.statement:
∀ (m r : Nat),
  let V := Fin m × Fin r
  let W := V → Bool
  let Symbol := Fin r → Bool
  let eval := fun (T : Finset (Finset V)) (w : W) =>
    (((T.filter (fun f => ∀ v ∈ f, w v = true)).card % 2) == 1)
  ∀ (terms : Finset (Finset V)) (U : Finset V), U ∈ terms →
    (∀ f ∈ terms, U ⊆ f → f = U) →
    let old := (Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun x => eval terms x = true)
    (∀ w : W, (U.powerset.filter (fun A =>
      eval terms (fun v => if v ∈ U then decide (v ∈ A) else w v) = true)).card % 2 = 1) ∧
    ∀ (K : Nat) (bad : Fin K → Fin m → Symbol),
      let gone := U.image Prod.fst
      let miss := fun (J : Finset (Fin m)) (word : W) =>
        ∀ a, ∃ i, i ∉ J ∧ (fun v => word (i,v)) = bad a i
      ((Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (miss gone)).card ≤
        2^U.card * (old.filter (miss ∅)).card
changed.unlocks: Charges projected list failures to support points using one maximal monomial.
changed.context: Fix every bit outside U and sum the polynomial over the bits of U in F2. Each term missing a variable of U cancels in pairs. Only U itself contains all of U, so the sum is one. A class that kills every entry on untouched blocks does so at all its 2^|U| members. Charge it to one support point in that class. Distinct classes charge distinct failures.
